taxonomy.note: Cryptovolans pauli is now considered the same animal as Microraptor.

diet.note: An opportunistic generalist: gut contents include a lizard (in M. zhaoianus), and a bird, fish and mammal remains in other Microraptor specimens (two of those studies were on specimens identified as M. gui).

timeRange.note: Aptian, from PBDB occurrence ages for M. zhaoianus in the Jiufotang Formation of Liaoning (stage-level dates).

text.en: Microraptor was a crow-sized feathered dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of north-eastern China, about 120 million years ago. It had wings on both its arms and its legs, and it could probably glide or even fly. Its feathers were black with a glossy, iridescent sheen. About 300 specimens are known, and some still hold their last meals: a bird, fish, a lizard and mammal bones.
When it was named in 2000, Microraptor was the first fully grown non-bird dinosaur known to be smaller than Archaeopteryx.
Tiny pigment structures in a Microraptor fossil suggest its plumage was mostly iridescent, with a glossy sheen.

uncertain.note: Two of the diet studies cited here used specimens identified as Microraptor gui. Whether M. gui is a separate species from M. zhaoianus was not checked against a primary source for this record.
